gloss: to throw in; to invest; to deploy

definitions.gloss: to throw in; to put in; to insert
definitions.explanation: To physically put something into a container, machine, or opening.

definitions.gloss: to invest; to commit (resources, effort, money)
definitions.explanation: To devote money, time, personnel, or other resources to a project or cause.

examples.japanese: コインを{投入|とうにゅう}する。
{自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}に{百円|ひゃくえん}を{投入|とうにゅう}した。
examples.english: I put a hundred yen into the vending machine.

examples.japanese: {釜|かま}に{材料|ざいりょう}を{次々|つぎつぎ}と{投入|とうにゅう}して{混|ま}ぜた。
examples.english: I threw ingredients into the pot one after another and mixed them.

examples.japanese: {資金|しきん}を{投入|とうにゅう}する。
{政府|せいふ}は{災害|さいがい}{復旧|ふっきゅう}に{大量|たいりょう}の{予算|よさん}を{投入|とうにゅう}した。
examples.english: The government invested a large budget in disaster recovery.

examples.japanese: この{事業|じぎょう}には{多|おお}くの{人材|じんざい}と{時間|じかん}が{投入|とうにゅう}されてきた。
examples.english: A great deal of human resources and time have been invested in this project.

notes:
A versatile verb used both for physically putting something into something and for committing resources. Sense 1 is concrete and literal; sense 2 is figurative and common in business, government, and news contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {資金|しきん}を{投入|とうにゅう}する: to invest funds
- {予算|よさん}を{投入|とうにゅう}する: to commit a budget
- {人員|じんいん}を{投入|とうにゅう}する: to deploy personnel
- コインを{投入|とうにゅう}する: to insert a coin
- {全力|ぜんりょく}を{投入|とうにゅう}する: to put in one's full effort

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {投資|とうし}する: to invest — specifically financial investment
- {注|つ}ぎ{込|こ}む: to pour into — more informal, emphasizes pouring effort or money
- {入|い}れる: to put in — the everyday general-purpose word
